1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

The rain in Qingshi had been falling for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu closed the door of the medicine shop and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two years old, and since her father's death she had been keeping the little shop going all on her own.
"Is anyone there?" A man's voice came from outside the door.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated for a moment, then opened the door. A young man stood in the doorway, soaked to the skin, his left hand clamped over his right arm, blood seeping out between his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need this bandaged," Chen Ziming said in a low voice. "I can pay — would a hundred and twenty yuan be enough?"

She didn't take his money. She simply had him sit down by the counter and turned to fetch gauze and medicinal wine. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if it had been sliced open by a blade. As she cleaned it, she asked him how he had been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent for a long while before he finally spoke. "I ran into some men on the road. They were after a letter I'm carrying." He drew an oilcloth-wrapped packet from inside his jacket and set it on the table. "This letter has to reach Baiyun before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun was up in the mountains, forty li from Qingshi, and mountain paths were at their worst in the rain. She remembered what her father used to say: if you're going to save someone, see it through to the end.
"First thing tomorrow morning, I'll take you up the mountain," she said. "Tonight you can sleep in the back room."
2: It was still dark when Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She shouldered her bamboo basket, which held dried rations, herbs, and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm had improved a little, but his face was still pale.
Halfway up the mountain, they ran into Zhou Dashan, the old woodcutter. Zhou Dashan knew Lin Xiaoyu, and he asked with a smile where she was headed so early.
"To Baiyun, to deliver medicine," Lin Xiaoyu answered. She didn't mention the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening, three men from out of town were at the town entrance asking about an injured young man. You two be careful."

Chen Ziming's face went even paler. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man, then led Chen Ziming off the main road and onto a trail known only to herb gatherers. The trail was narrow and slick. She walked in front, setting each foot down firmly.

By noon, the rain had finally stopped. The mountain mist slowly lifted, and the rooftops of Baiyun appeared in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate. Her name was Zhao Qiuyue, and she was in charge of receiving visitors.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper package, examined the red seal on the wrapping, and nodded. "My master has been waiting 2 years for this letter," she said. "You must be tired."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come to Qingshi, you can help me fix the roof of my medicine shop."
